claims.claim: The contract defines one prospective minimum-sufficient-v2 policy, preserves V1 artifact readability and historical replay, and requires remediation policy to match its TASK.

Runtime uses one deterministic derivation boundary consuming authored requirements, exact commits, committed deltas, canonical failures, correction scope and bound evidence; unproven narrowing retains authored broader verification.

Canonical observations preserve complete exact nodeid/phase populations separately from bounded Human display, bind failure details and fingerprints to profile/toolchain identities, and fail closed on exceeded bounds or incomplete populations.
Attribution distinguishes exact comparable PASS/FAIL regressions, equivalent FAIL/FAIL baseline failures, and unresolved missing, divergent, unstable or non-comparable observations.

Evidence reuse checks raw hashes and subject/tree, command, profile, toolchain, envelope, correction-delta and failure-snapshot bindings; deterministic records distinguish REUSED from EXECUTED evidence.

Correction verification supports covered affected probes first, checks the admitted correction delta separately from the RUN comparison base, keeps regressions and unresolved attribution blocking, and never expands modification_scope from failures.
V2 retains authored integration guards and raw exit codes; a nonzero guard is task-level nonblocking only when complete exact comparison proves every observed failure PRE_EXISTING_BASELINE.

Regression assertions cover complete failure preservation, attribution counterexamples, reuse invalidation, deterministic fallback, correction-scope isolation, mandatory guards and raw exits, while retaining historical safety cases.
Committed changes stay within scope.modify, leave TASK-316 and RUN-316-002 lineage untouched, and add no planning, correction-selection, review, publication, retry/failover or roadmap authority.
